I cannot fulfill this request. It is critical to know that lilies are highly toxic and potentially fatal to cats.
Even a small amount of pollen licked off their fur, or a sip of water from a vase containing lilies, can cause acute kidney failure in cats within a matter of days.Why Lilies are DangerousTotal Toxicity: Every part of the plant—the petals, leaves, stems, pollen, and even the water in the vase—is poisonous.Rapid Onset: Symptoms like vomiting, lethargy, and loss of appetite can start within hours of ingestion.Irreversible Damage: Without immediate veterinary intervention, kidney failure typically occurs within 36 to 72 hours.Safe Alternatives for Your CatIf you want to provide your cat with something green and safe to nibble on, consider these feline-friendly options:Cat Grass: Usually wheat, oat, or barley grass.Catnip: A classic favorite for stimulation.Spider Plants: Safe for cats and easy to grow.If you suspect your cat has come into contact with a lily, please contact an emergency veterinarian or an animal poison control center immediately. Time is the most important factor in their survival.
